# Disentangling Ambiguity from Instability in Large Language Models: A Clinical Text-to-SQL Case Study

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#clues)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://aclanthology.org/2026.clinicalnlp-1.39.pdf) · ClinicalNLP at LREC 2026 proceedings, pages 369-380

**Reading coverage:** All substantive Sections 1-8 on PDF pages 1-9, equations 1-3, Figure 1, Tables 1-6; remaining pages are references. No appendices in this version.

## Research question

Output diversity may reflect legitimate interpretation differences or unreliable generation under one interpretation; these require different interventions.

## Method

CLUES builds interpretation and answer similarity matrices plus provenance links. Heat-kernel entropy measures ambiguity; a regularized Schur complement with PSD projection yields an operational conditional-instability score. Median splits define four routing regimes.

## Evaluation

Open QA uses gold interpretations. The clinical study uses 109 questions, five models and four temperatures, with controlled interpretations followed by a generated-interpretation deployment configuration. Answers and similarities are judged by LLMs; clinical SQL runs on a restricted Optum database.

## What the results support

Conditional instability improves pooled known-interpretation clinical AUROC from 0.600 to 0.762. In the deployment setup its AUROC is 0.648 versus 0.687 for result entropy, a nonsignificant difference. The compound regime contains 48 of 95 failures across pooled configurations.

## Limits and qualifications

Generated interpretations, similarity judgments, thresholds and repeated model/question instances shape the results. Routing is analyzed retrospectively; benefits of actual clarification or human review are not tested. Section 5.2 alternately describes a gold interpretation plus three alternatives and a three-interpretation/nine-query setup.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides diagnostic separation rather than a validated clinical safety or automatic-routing guarantee.
